issue.title: Accept statements separated by semicolons
issue.body:
Our bank in Zurich exports CSV with semicolons between the columns, which is
also what Excel uses with Swiss settings. Amounts use a dot for decimals, and I
renamed the header to `date;amount;description`, but the upload is rejected at
row 1 with 'Malformed row: the number of columns does not match the header'.
Replacing every semicolon with a comma makes the file import, but that breaks
descriptions that contain commas. Could the upload accept semicolon-separated
files too?
## Discussion

### lena-k (maintainer) · 2026-11-06
Do your bank's files ever mix the two, or is it always semicolons?

### zurich-treasury-ab · 2026-11-06
Always semicolons, for both our accounts there. A description is in double
quotes when it contains a semicolon.

input.title: Accept semicolon-separated statement files in the parser
input.body:
File: src/ingest/parser.ts

parseStatement and splitFields hard-code the comma as the field delimiter: the header is split with split(",") and splitFields only treats "," as a separator. Detect the delimiter from the header line (a semicolon when the header contains ";" and no ","; otherwise a comma), and pass it to splitFields so the header and every data row are split with the same delimiter. Quoted fields keep working as they do now, so a description in double quotes can contain the delimiter.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

Thanks for the detailed report; here is what triage found.

The parser hard-codes the comma as the field separator: parseStatement splits the header with split(",") and splitFields only treats "," as a delimiter, so a semicolon header is read as one column and the row check fails. The parser already exports a DEFAULT_DELIMITER constant, so the detected value can simply replace it. The draft change detects the delimiter from the header and uses it for every row, keeping quoted fields intact.

In short: the parser hard-codes the comma as the field separator: parseStatement splits the header with split(",") and splitFields only treats "," as a delimiter, so a semicolon header is read as one column and the row check fails.

This triage rests on the issue as it was filed and on what RepoMind's own reads of the repository returned. If any of it looks wrong, a maintainer can change the label or close the draft pull request. Nothing has been merged.
